fullPassage: To monitor our surroundings is to focus on what's outside of ourselves: what we see, hear, smell, feel, and perhaps even taste. But sometimes what really marks a place is something less specific — a feeling within us. An interesting example emerged from a study of subway passenger behavior. Researchers trying to understand why people sit where they sit or stand where they stand in subway and metro trains examined the factors that shape the way riders used and navigated that space in different situations. One of their findings involved the reasons many riders like to plant themselves close to the train's doors. But it was shaped partly by a more abstract sensation — the desire to avoid the sometimes uncomfortable feeling of accidentally making eye contact with seated passengers. We can't see feelings — but they're very real, and they influence our experience of the world.

det.analysis: 마지막 문장: We can't see feelings — but they're very real, and they influence our experience of the world. → 6단어 답: influence our experience of the world.
det.tip: influence our experience of the world

questions.wa: influence our experience of the world
accept: influence our experience of the world

questions.passage: To monitor our surroundings is to focus on what's outside of ourselves: what we see, hear, smell, feel, and perhaps even taste. But sometimes what really marks a place is something less specific — a feeling within us. An interesting example emerged from a study of subway passenger behavior. Researchers trying to understand why people sit where they sit or stand where they stand in subway and metro trains examined the factors that shape the way riders used and navigated that space in different situations. One of their findings involved the reasons many riders like to plant themselves close to the train's doors. But it was shaped partly by a more abstract sensation — the desire to avoid the sometimes uncomfortable feeling of accidentally making eye contact with seated passengers. We can't see feelings — but they're very real, and they influence our experience of the world.
questions.stem: 위 글에서 장소를 특별하게 만드는 것이 때로는 구체적인 것이 아닌 무엇이라고 했는지 본문에서 찾아 쓰시오. (영어로) (3단어)

det.korean: a feeling within us (내면의 감정). 장소를 특별하게 만드는 것은 덜 구체적인 — 내면의 감정.
det.analysis: 원문: what really marks a place is something less specific — a feeling within us. → 구체적이지 않은 것 = a feeling within (us).
det.tip: a feeling within us = 내면의 감정

questions.stem: 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 주제: 눈에 보이지 않는 감정이 장소 경험에 미치는 영향.
det.analysis:
① 감정이 장소 경험에 미치는 영향: 본문 핵심 — feelings influence experience ← 정답
② 지하철 설계와 편의: 본문은 설계가 아닌 감정에 관한 글 ❌
③ 좌석 배치: 좌석 자체가 아닌 감정이 핵심 ❌
④ 감각 기관의 과학적 원리: 감각 인식이 아닌 내면 감정이 핵심 ❌
det.tip: feelings influence our experience of the world

questions.stem: 다음 글의 요지로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 요지: 장소 경험은 외부 감각뿐 아니라 눈에 보이지 않는 내면 감정에 의해서도 형성된다.
